why: Found at the build's test run after the versioned model was regenerated: the key's thresholds.inputs_sha256 pins gen/M3/versions/models/morph_rollup.versions.init.json at the base's sha256 (I28's model debt record, the debt I83 pays), but that file lies under the key's own outcome_paths (gen/M3/versions/models/) and P1 requires it to change (every version's debt empty). The pin documents the base's input, and the instrument (tests_m3/_i83.py) never reads the file. The amended test compares a pinned input under one of the key's outcome_paths with its content at thresholds.base_commit, and every other pinned input with the tree, as before. No prediction, threshold or other test changes.

Found when I29's build merged into the I83 branch (064ddec4, the lead 918b9a4e): I29's NAT records name the NAT claims module gen/M3/nat/models/morph_rollup_nat.bend, not the versioned layer (holon.rules.nat_run writes model_sha256 as the sha256 of the claims module), so the clause 'its model_sha256, when it names one, is the layer's' cannot hold for a correct record. The coordinator's decision, with its conditions: a record whose model_sha256 names the NAT claims module counts only if that module imports I83's current layer file, sha-verified through the confined resolver (holon.statement_diff._model_files: the layer file the module reaches hashes to the sha256 of the layer's link target), and the record was re-made after the merge that brought I29's build (its last first-parent change is a later commit than the one that added the law, and descends from it). A record naming the layer is checked as before, and the status must be UNKNOWN as before. No prediction, threshold or other test changes.

Found when I29's build merged into the I83 branch (064ddec4, the lead 918b9a4e): I83-P6's claim names I29's NAT laws among the laws bound to the versioned layer once its build has merged ("the PAR-init law; and I29's NAT laws once its build has merged"), but the test selects only the bindings whose model is the layer's link. A NAT law's binding names the NAT claims module gen/M3/nat/models/morph_rollup_nat.bend, which imports the layer, so the test's set leaves out the laws the claim includes and fails on the NAT laws' model_extension lines the claim requires. The amended test also counts a binding whose model imports I83's current layer file, sha-verified through the confined resolver (holon.statement_diff._model_files), the condition of I83-P5's amendment: the set is then the PAR-init law and the 9 NAT laws, as the claim says. Every other assertion is unchanged; no prediction, threshold or other test changes.
